authorship.author: v3_training_author
authorship.method: Human-review draft of bounded wording substitutions in the existing 64 D5 option-training rows; no independent evaluation or human approval is claimed.

sources.selection: D5, bucket clarity, split train; original 48 option rows

scope.operational_changes: Draft file only. No training data, model architecture, model parameters, validators, all15/default configuration, model artifacts or runtime changes are made by this file.

design_justification: Use a bounded set of 15 base-row edits: eight rows share current living expenses across the eight options; seven replace everyday with day-to-day because salary already has unchanged day-to-day anchors. The remaining 49 rows stay verbatim.

Retain named source distinctions, such as sole-trader versus consultancy income, savings account versus investment withdrawals, pension payments, benefits plus family support, rental receipts and explicit absence of a regular source.

All 16 v1/v2 additions remain verbatim, including short anchors, excluded wages or savings, future pension, stopped earning, two jobs in one category, and two active categories. The proposal does not simplify these contrasts into direct-source templates.

Monthly income timing, current-month expenditure and partial-use language are preserved only where stated originally. The draft does not force those styles into every category because doing so would add unsupported facts.

The supplied qualitative diagnosis motivates wording distribution only. No probabilities, fitting, predictions or evaluation outputs informed these substitutions, and no performance improvement is claimed.
review_limits: This draft requires human approval of original and proposed wording before any training.
Equivalence of everyday/day-to-day and current living costs/current living expenses is proposed for human business review, not certified by an independent evaluator.
Some source-category wording remains uneven where the original semantics do not permit a frequency or partial-use substitution.
Existing semantically related examples are retained; the draft intentionally preserves source details and exclusions rather than claiming all original rows are semantically unique.

Retained original source annotations describe historical pre-approval states, including D5-LT-01 and the v2 rows. The hash-bound v1 and v2 human-review records already approved those original texts and labels. Their original provenance is retained; it does not approve this new v3 wording proposal.

source_access_disclosure.deviation: The first train.csv extraction filtered D5 without the clarity condition and exposed eight additional non-clear training rows, IDs SYNTH-V1-D5-TRAIN-049 through SYNTH-V1-D5-TRAIN-056. The mistake was reported to the parent agent before drafting.
source_access_disclosure.effect: Those eight rows are excluded from this file and were not used to choose wording changes. Subsequent training-row extraction was limited to the authorised 64 clarity rows.
source_access_disclosure.restricted_material: No calibration, validation, model artifacts, compare/evaluation result contents or prior experiment probabilities were opened. Only filenames were listed while locating the equivalent business standard; the authorised business standard itself contains existing case expectations.
